reports.title: Targa Resources Corp. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Announces Expectation for a 20% Increase to its 2027 Common Dividend

guidance.heading: 2026 Outlook and Capital Allocation Update
section: Given the strength of Targa’s operating performance through the first three quarters of the year, Targa now estimates full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA to be at least $6.0 billion. We continue to estimate net growth capital expenditures to be approximately $5.0 billion, and our estimate for 2026 net maintenance capital expenditures remains unchanged at approximately $250 million.

For the first quarter of 2027, management intends to recommend to Targa’s Board of Directors an increase to its common dividend to $1.50 per common share or $6.00 per common share annualized. The recommended common dividend per share increase, if approved, would be effective for the first quarter of 2027 and payable in May 2027. Beyond 2027, we expect to be in position to continue to provide meaningful annual increases to our common dividend.
An earnings supplement presentation and updated investor presentation are available under Events and Presentations in the Investors section of our website at www.targaresources.com/investors/events.

desk.headline: Adjusted EBITDA up 18% to $1.5bn on record Permian volumes; 2026 EBITDA now seen at $6.0bn or more, 20% dividend rise planned for 2027
results: Revenue rose 35% to $5.6bn and adjusted EBITDA 18% to $1.5bn, though EBITDA fell 6% from Q2 as marketing and LPG export margins eased.
Gathering and processing margin rose 22% on record Permian gas volumes of 7.54 Bcf/d, up 14%, with the Delaware basin up 20%.
Record NGL pipeline and fractionation volumes lifted logistics margin 10%.
Heavy building spending ($1.2bn of growth capex in the quarter) cut adjusted free cash flow to $34m; debt stood at $19.8bn.
Targa paid a $1.25 quarterly dividend, up 25%, and bought back $52m of shares.

guidance.summary: Targa now expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA of at least $6.0bn, an increase on its earlier outlook, but published sources disagree on the earlier range so it is not shown. Growth capex stays at about $5.0bn, and management plans to propose a 20% dividend rise to $6.00 a share for 2027.

points: Management said Targa's Permian volumes grew about 13% this year, roughly twice the basin as a whole.
Marketing gains of about $250m in the first half faded in Q3 as fewer trading opportunities came up.
The new 20-year ExxonMobil deal underpins three new Delaware plants; management admitted Exxon pushed hard on price.
Leverage held at about 3.4x and spending will stay high into 2027 as new plants and a 14th fractionation train are built.
call.source: Earnings Whispers, Targa Q3 2026 earnings, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether 2027 capex stays near 2026 levels, delaying a pick-up in free cash flow.
Start-up of the Copperhead plant and Train 12, and timing of the Yeti plants in 2027.
Marketing and LPG export margins after their Q3 drop.
